title: Open Model Catalog Harmonization & Pipeline Demo
meeting_header: Date: 2026-08-18 | Time: 14:00 PDT | Duration: 54m | Redwood: Jamie Collins, Priya Shah | Stratus Studio: Liam Wong, Aisha Patel, Marco Diaz
summary: AE+SE walk through the open model catalog, compatibility matrix and bench interpretation for Stratus Studio's content-generation pipeline. Discussed selection heuristics, latency/cost tradeoffs, private deployment constraints and next steps to run a short pilot benchmark with customer's prompts.
topics: Benchmarks: throughput vs latency vs quality
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Collins: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jamie from Redwood inference, with Priya our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Liam Wong: Liam here, hi.
[00:10] Aisha Patel: Aisha on my side.
[00:12] Marco Diaz: Marco, thanks.
[00:15] Jamie Collins: Great. We're planning 45-ish minutes demo and 10 for q&a. Agenda on the deck: catalog walk, compatibility matrix, bench interpretation, then pipeline options.
[02:18] Priya Shah: (screen share starts) Alright I'm in the Console, so first thing, model catalog landing page. You'll see filters across model family, sequence length, quantization support and hardware compatibility. Quick note: our auto-detected compat is heuristics plus our runtime tests so sometimes the name mapping is slightly off, eg we show "LLM-X-Quant" as compatible with A100v4 but the kernel path might favor T4 in some seq lengths — you'll see that in the matrix.
[05:40] Liam Wong: Quick question—do you show per-model tokenization differences? We have issues with tokenization causing latency spikes.
[05:52] Priya Shah: Yes we surface tokenizer family and expected average token expansion for typical English prompts. It's an estimate. Also we annotate KV cache memory for multi-turns; sometimes the export labels it as K-V cache but that's the same thing.
[07:20] Marco Diaz: Can you filter by licensing? We only want permissive licenses.
[07:28] Priya Shah: Yep, license char filters. We'll also call out models that require additional review.
[08:45] Jamie Collins: Moving to the compatibility matrix: this is more of a many-to-many matrix — models on rows, runtime variants on columns. Cells contain benchmark fingerprints: latency p95, throughput at batch size x, and a quick quality note from our evals.
[12:20] Priya Shah: (zooming) See this cell — this model was run with 4k context, int8 quant, and shows a significant latency jump after 1k tokens — that's due to attention kernel fallback. We highlight kernel-fallback rows in orange.
[15:30] Aisha Patel: How do you rank recommended model variants? We have a strict 250ms p95 SLO for inline generation.
[15:41] Priya Shah: Good point. The catalog has a recommendation score computed from: match to target task, p95 latency margin relative to SLO, tokens-per-dollar cost estimate, and stability (variance across batch shapes). You can weight those factors in the Console.
[18:10] Liam Wong: About the bench results — our team saw very different outputs when we re-ran bench with our prompts vs the vendor's seed prompts. How should we interpret your 'quality' tag?
[18:25] Jamie Collins: The short answer: treat quality tags as directional. We run curated evals and hold-out prompt baskets to estimate degradation between variants. For fidelity you should run a short prompt-specific bench. We'll help with the harness.
[20:05] Priya Shah: Now the Bench interpretation tab: here's the comparison chart — latency vs quality delta. Note the x-axis quality delta is our composite (ROUGE-ish + human-ish quick checks). There are noisy points because open model outputs vary.
[22:00] Marco Diaz: Curious about cost math — do you assume batching? Our workload is low QPS but high concurrency of short requests.
[22:12] Priya Shah: The cost-per-token calc shows two scenarios: continuous batching (good for steady QPS) and on-demand (small batch sizes). For short requests the per-call overhead dominates, so smaller models or optimized kernels are usually better. We also show a suggested batching policy in Redwood Optimize (we label it "Opti" in some exports, sorry the transcript says Redwood Opti sometimes).
[25:40] Priya Shah: Demo: selecting two candidate models, adding them to a shortlist, and creating a bench run. You can upload your prompt set; we support multi-file CSV or a zipped corpus.
[28:10] Liam Wong: For our internal requirements we need private deployment in our VPC and KMS keys for all assets. Does the bench run require data to leave our VPC?
[28:25] Jamie Collins: If you choose Private deployment mode the bench can run inside your VPC with our private agent. We support customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. For hosted bench runs we can mask tokens and you can review logs; it's one of those tradeoffs.
[30:05] Aisha Patel: SOC2 + ISO status? We need the paperwork for procurement.
[30:12] Jamie Collins: We are SOC2 Type II and have ISO docs — I'll share the packet. Also we have SSO SAML integrations with SCIM for provisioning.
[32:00] Priya Shah: Back to the compatibility matrix: note that the matrix will suggest fallback variants for when a chosen variant hits capacity constraints — fallback could be a quantized variant or a regionally proximate model. You can set fallback rules per route and per customer tier.
[34:40] Marco Diaz: How much variance do you see when switching quantization methods? Our bench showed a big quality delta between int8 and int4 on some tasks.
[34:52] Priya Shah: It depends on model architecture and task. Our suggestion engine will mark high-risk quantization combos; we also keep example divergence logs in the evals tab so you can inspect difference-by-prompt.
[36:30] Liam Wong: For the pilot, can we pin model versions and avoid automatic upgrades during evaluation?
[36:38] Jamie Collins: Absolutely — pinning is supported per route. We also provide a canary rollout flow for incremental traffic.
[38:10] Aisha Patel: Pricing — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated for a small pilot?
[38:20] Jamie Collins: For pilots we usually recommend hosted (per-token) to move faster. Dedicated is a reserved commitment — for small pilots hosted is simpler and lower up-front. We'll send a simple price comparator sheet after the call.
[40:00] Priya Shah: Quick live walkthrough of Redwood Console's Optimize recommendations: it surfaced that for your short prompt distribution, a smaller model with aggressive caching and 2-3 token prefix cache hits gives better tokens-per-dollar than a single large model. The Optimize tool also suggests kernel flags and batch shapes.
[42:50] Marco Diaz: Data residency — we operate in EMEA only. Can you restrict region and run benches in that region?
[43:00] Jamie Collins: Yes, you can restrict regions at the project level; bench runs will use the region you select. For Private we can deploy on-prem or in your VPC region.
[45:20] Liam Wong: Any competitors we should be aware of from a benching perspective?
[45:27] Priya Shah: A few: Anthropic does closed-model endpoints, Vertex AI has benching tools, and SageMaker offers managed endpoints — but our differentiation is the model catalog blending open models + runtime-verified compat + routing/Optimize tooling.
[47:10] Aisha Patel: Ok let's go over next steps.
[47:15] Jamie Collins: Recap — we'll share: bench template, catalog export with the shortlist, security docs, and a pricing comparator. Priya will help run the pilot bench inside the 48-hour window once you upload prompts.
[48:30] Marco Diaz: Sounds good. I'd like to lock in a pilot start next week if possible.
[48:40] Jamie Collins: We can do that — Priya, are you able to schedule?
[48:44] Priya Shah: Yes I'll send a calendar invite for a 1 hour pilot kickoff and a 2 day bench window.
[49:05] Liam Wong: One last thing: how do we handle model auditability — we need to keep diffs of outputs after rollouts for compliance.
[49:15] Jamie Collins: We store eval snapshots per run, plus per-route output capture if you opt in. Those artifacts can be exported to your S3 or internal storage with encryption.
[50:00] Aisha Patel: Perfect. Thanks team.
[50:05] Marco Diaz: Thanks Jamie, Priya.
[50:07] Jamie Collins: Thank you all. We'll follow up with the docs and the bench spreadsheet.
[52:10] (call ends)

Priya to schedule pilot kickoff and bench window (48-hour run) and send calendar invite
Stratus to upload representative prompt set and target SLOs before kickoff
